text:
sasha: quick question — do we want the gateway to be able to preempt long-running streaming requests when we need capacity for higher-priority traffic? thinking about mobile low-latency customers vs background batch chat sessions.

matt: short answer: maybe, but tradeoffs. preemption can violate at-least-once semantics for side-effecting streams. also billing + user expectations. :thinking:

priya: agree. key Qs: how to signal preemptability from client? how to surface retry semantics in API? and what about partial-response checkpoints so we can resume or reassign work?

dave: implementation sketch: attach a preempt token + optional checkpointing header. gateway can cancel and persist a lightweight checkpoint (k/v cache) and then resume on another worker if the model supports it. if no checkpoint -> fall back to graceful cancel and return trailer with "preempted" reason.

sasha: example headers i've been tossing around:

```
X-Request-Priority: high|normal|background
X-Preempt-Token: opaque-uuid-1234
X-Checkpoint-Policy: none|kv-checkpoint|fullstate
```

sasha: and trailers when preempted: `grpc-status=4, preempt-reason=capacity` or `http/1.1 499 Preempted`?

priya: prefer structured trailers so SDKs can react. 499 is confusing. grpc trailer + `preempt-token` for resume looks good. sdk flow: if trailer includes `preempt-token` && checkpoint policy active -> automatically attempt resume (with idempotency guard)

matt: important: resume attempts count as retries for billing and quota. we should avoid silent double-charges. maybe an idempotency header `X-Resume-Id` and server marks resumed bytes as continuing rather than new.

carol: SLO angle: preempting a low-priority streaming request reduces tail latency for high-priority but increases error rate for preempted ones. need to expose preempt rate metric per customer + SLA opt-outs. enterprise tenants should be able to opt-out of preemption.

dave: ops considerations: preempting mid-stream risks KV cache inconsistency (kv cache may hold per-stream context). we either need a durable checkpoint store (latency/cost) or accept only prefix-based resume for short-window preemptions.

priya: maybe we define two preempt modes: 
- soft-preempt: pause and hold reservation for X seconds (short window)
- hard-preempt: cancel and emit preempt-token for resume later (may cost more to resume)

sasha: UX for clients: SDK default should be `no-resume` for simple customers. enable `resume_on_preempt=true` per-request for advanced flows. docs show code: `client.generate({resumeOnPreempt: true, checkpointPolicy: 'kv-checkpoint'})`

matt: security: preempt-token must be signed and short-lived, otherwise risk of token replay/resume by other tenants. also gate resume to same customer project id.

ops-bot: deploy queued: probot/edge-preempt-proto v2 -> canary to region-us-west-2 at 2025-09-15T18:00Z

carol: telemetry: record `preempt.event` with fields: priority, preempt_reason, checkpoint_policy, bytes_emitted, resumed (bool), resume_latency_ms. expose as per-customer dashboard.

dave: edge-level admission: admission controller should consider preemptable capacity separately so non-preemptable pools don't get starved. i propose separate admission queues: `nonpreempt` and `preemptable` with token buckets.

priya: recovery semantics: if resume fails (missing checkpoint or model mismatch) return a clear error `PREEMPT_RESUME_FAILED` with guidance. sdk should bubble this as a retriable or non-retriable depending on client choice.

sasha: outstanding decisions we need to lock:
- header names and exact trailer format
- billing semantics for resume attempts (count vs continue)
- opt-out policy / enterprise flagging
- whether to support full state checkpointing or restrict to prefix/kv snapshots

matt: proposed defaults: `X-Checkpoint-Policy=kv-checkpoint` optional; resume attempts are charged as continuation (not full new request) if resume_token present and server accepts continuation. otherwise charged as new.

carol: +1 on exposing preempt metrics and opt-out. also add a per-customer `preempt_threshold` (0-100%) to control percent of sessions eligible for preemption.

dave: note: tests we need: chaos test where we preempt 30% of background streams while flooding high-priority traffic and verify tail latency improvement and resume correctness.

sasha: ok i'll draft a small RFC with API examples, trailers, and a telemetry schema. i'll include the cost model proposal for resume billing. ping me if you want items on the RFC checklist. :+1:

matt: add me as reviewer. happy to sketch admission controller token-bucket config.

priya: i'll sketch SDK behaviour for resume/backoff.

carol: put enterprise opt-out in RBAC + tenant config UI.

sasha: thanks all — i'll post the RFC link here when ready.
